Beriev A-50: Russia. Developed to replace the Tupolev Tu-126 "Moss", the A-50 first flew in 1978.
Who is credited with discovering Fructose?
Fructose: Augustin-Pierre Dubrunfaut. Fructose, or fruit sugar, is a common monosaccharide, i.e. a simple sugar.
Who is credited with discovering LSD?
LSD: Albert Hofmann. LSD taken orally has an onset of action of 0.4 to 1.0 hours and a duration of 7 to 12 hours.
Who is credited with discovering Manganese?
Manganese: Johan Gottlieb Gahn. Manganese is a chemical element; it has the symbol Mn and atomic number 25.
Often confused with the unrelated sweet chestnut, this large deciduous tree in the maple, soapberry, and lychee family bears hermaphroditic flowers — what tree is it?
Aesculus hippocastanum is a species of flowering plant in the maple, soapberry and lychee family Sapindaceae.
In this group of diseases, misfolded proteins clump into fibrils and accumulate in body tissue, sometimes causing an enlarged tongue or carpal tunnel syndrome — name the condition?
Amyloidosis is a group of diseases in which abnormal proteins, known as amyloid fibrils, build up in tissue.
This discipline studies past human activity by recovering and analyzing artifacts, architecture, and other material remains through surveying and excavation — name the field?
Archaeology is the study of human activity through the recovery and analysis of material culture.
Native to the Mekong and Chao Phraya river basins, this freshwater catfish is marketed in the US as "swai" and in the UK as "river cobbler" — which fish?

Basa (fish) (Pangasius bocourti), as it is commonly referred to, is a species of primarily freshwater-dwelling catfish in the shark-catfish family, Pangasiidae, native to the Mekong and Chao Phraya river basins of Mainland Southeast Asia.
A flowering vine native to South Asia, this plant's small dried red drupes become the world's most traded spice, its final coloring depending on how ripe the fruit was when harvested — which spice?
Black pepper (Piper nigrum) is a flowering vine in the family Piperaceae, cultivated for its fruit (the peppercorn), which is usually dried and used as a spice and seasoning.
An Austrian-born psychologist who directed Chicago's Orthogenic School, he was an early and controversial writer on autism whose ideas grew out of Freud — who was he?

Bruno Bettelheim (August 28, 1903 - March 13, 1990) was an Austrian-born American psychologist, scholar, public intellectual and writer who spent most of his academic and clinical career in the United States.
A child prodigy who became director of the Göttingen Observatory, this German polymath left his mark on number theory, algebra, geometry, statistics, and probability alike — who is he?
Carl Friedrich Gauss (30 April 1777 - 23 February 1855) was a German mathematician, astronomer, geodesist, and physicist, who contributed to many fields in mathematics and science.
A sweet-smelling, dense, colorless liquid with the formula CHCl3, this solvent doubled as an inhaled anesthetic from the 19th century into the early 20th. What is it?
Chloroform (often abbreviated as TCM), is an organochloride with the formula CHCl3 and a common solvent.
A true thrush of Europe, western Asia and North Africa, the male of its nominate subspecies is entirely black — and depending on latitude it may stay put or migrate. What bird is it?
Common blackbird (Turdus merula) is a species of true thrush.
The third most-produced American fighter of the Second World War, trailing only the Mustang and the Thunderbolt, this plane first took flight in 1938 — which aircraft?
Curtiss P-40 Warhawk is an American single-engined, single-seat, all-metal fighter-bomber that first flew in 1938.
Sucrose, lactose, and maltose are the best-known examples of this water-soluble carbohydrate class, each formed by linking two simple sugars together — what's the term?
Disaccharide (also called a double sugar or biose) is the sugar formed when two monosaccharides are joined by glycosidic linkage.
Which American toy magnate teamed up with his wife Ruth to co-found Mattel and dream up Hot Wheels and Barbie?
Elliot Handler (April 9, 1916 - July 21, 2011) was an American inventor, business magnate, and the co-founder of Mattel.
This term describes the practice of exposing normally covered body parts to others in public or semi-public settings, whether in person or via a nude photo shared digitally — what is it?
Exhibitionism is the practice of exposing one's intimate parts - such as the breasts, genitals, or buttocks - in a public or semi-public environment.
Sitting just below caesium as the second-most electropositive element, this alkali metal decays so fast that a bulk sample has never actually been seen — what is it?
Francium is a chemical element; it has symbol Fr and atomic number 87.

Encoded by the codons CAA and CAG and structurally related to glutamic acid but with an amide in place of a carboxylic acid group, this charge-neutral amino acid becomes essential under bodily stress — which amino acid?
Glutamine (symbol Gln or Q) is an -amino acid that is used in the biosynthesis of proteins.

Element 108's isotope 270 carries magic numbers of protons and neutrons that shore it up against fission, yet the most stable forms last only about ten seconds — which synthetic superheavy element is it?
Hassium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Hs and atomic number 108.
Running from the shoulder to the elbow, this arm bone connects the scapula to the radius and ulna, with a rounded head and neck at one end and two epicondyles at the other — name this bone?
Humerus (pl.: humeri) is a long bone in the arm that runs from the shoulder to the elbow.
This Belgian-American physicist-mathematician and 1992 MacArthur Fellow is best known for harnessing wavelets to compress images — a tool so foundational it bears her name. Who is she?
Ingrid Daubechies (doh-bə-SHEE; born 17 August 1954) is a Belgian-American physicist and mathematician at Duke University.
This American physicist revived general relativity in postwar America and had a knack for naming things — coining "quantum foam," "wormhole," and the term "black hole" itself. Who is he?
John Archibald Wheeler (July 9, 1911 - April 13, 2008) was an American theoretical physicist.
This Arab dessert layers spun pastry dough with cheese, soaked in a sugar syrup, with its most famous variant hailing from the Palestinian city of Nablus — what is it?
Knafeh is a traditional Arab dessert made with kadayif (spun pastry dough) layered with cheese and soaked in a sweet, sugar-based syrup called attar.
This genus of large-flowered bulb plants is prized in gardens worldwide but is highly toxic to cats. What genus is it?
Lilium is a genus of herbaceous flowering plants growing from bulbs, all with large and often prominent flowers.
Members of the family Scombridae, these open-ocean fish sport forked tails and green-blue tiger stripes, often wintering in deep water after a coastal spawning run — what fish are they?
Mackerel is a common name applied to a number of different species of pelagic fish, mostly from the family Scombridae.
Raised in Wilmington, Delaware by Turkish immigrant parents, this cardiac surgeon co-founded a complementary-care center for heart patients before finding fame on television — who is he?

Mehmet Oz (mə-MET JENG-ghiz oz; born June 11, 1960), also known as Dr. Oz, is an American television presenter, physician, author, educator, and government official serving as the 17th administrator of the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) since 2025.

An Egyptian who studied architecture at Cairo University and worked as a civil engineer, this man was the oldest of the 19 hijackers and the ringleader who piloted American Airlines Flight 11 into the North Tower — who was he?
Mohamed Atta (September 1, 1968 - September 11, 2001) was an Egyptian engineer, architect, and the lead terrorist hijacker for al-Qaeda on American Airlines Flight 11.

Which form of alternative medicine, rooted in vitalism and folk healing rather than evidence, gathers 'natural' and 'self-healing' practices ranging from discredited homeopathy to accepted psychotherapy?
Naturopathy is a form of alternative medicine. The ethics of naturopathy have been called into question by medical professionals and its practice has been characterized as quackery.
First described by Linnaeus in 1758, this medium-sized spotted cat of the Americas is a skilled climber, leaper, and swimmer that hunts armadillos and opossums by night — which cat is it?
Ocelot (Leopardus pardalis) is a medium-sized spotted wild cat that reaches 40-50 cm (16-20 in) at the shoulders and weighs between 7 and 15.5 kg (15 and 34 lb) on average.
Contrasted with 'normophilic' interests and famously tallied at up to 549 types by Anil Aggrawal, this contested clinical category covers atypical sexual attraction — what's its name?
Paraphilia is an uncommon, intense, and persistent sexual arousal or attraction to anything not sexual by nature, though preference is favored for specific designations.
Members of the family Phasianidae and native to Eurasia, these game birds snack on insects and fresh green shoots come summer — what are they?
Pheasant are birds of several genera within the family Phasianidae in the order Galliformes.
Built from poetic devices like onomatopoeia, rhyme schemes, and rhythm, this literary art uses the musical qualities of language to suggest more than the words plainly say — what is it?

Poetry (from the Greek word poiesis, "making") is a form of literary art that uses aesthetic and often rhythmic qualities of language to evoke meanings in addition to, or in place of, literal or surface-level meanings.
Found in more than 200 species of mushroom, this inactive compound is a prodrug your body quickly converts to psilocin, a near-cousin of serotonin — what is it?
Psilocybin (4-), is a naturally occurring tryptamine alkaloid and investigational drug found in more than 200 species of mushrooms, with hallucinogenic and serotonergic effects.
This rapidly worsening brain condition can follow a bout of chickenpox or influenza and is strongly associated with aspirin use in children — what syndrome is it?
Reye syndrome is a rapidly worsening brain disease. Signs and symptoms of Reye syndrome may include vomiting, personality changes, confusion, seizures, and loss of consciousness.
A Stanford physicist who also held an English literature degree, in 1983 she became, at 32, the youngest American ever to fly in space. Who is she?
Sally Ride (May 26, 1951-July 23, 2012) was an American astronaut and physicist.
Until 2010, this pungent little cultivar of the onion was classified as its own species before being folded back into the common onion — name this allium?
Shallot is a cultivar group of the onion. Until 2010, the (French red) shallot was classified as a separate species, Allium ascalonicum.
These eight-legged arachnids inject venom through their fangs and extrude silk from spinnerets, ranking as the largest order in their class — what are they?
Spider (order Araneae) are air-breathing arthropods that have eight limbs, chelicerae with fangs generally able to inject venom, and spinnerets that extrude silk.
A starchy tuber from the morning-glory family, often confused with yams in North America despite being only distantly related to them — what root vegetable is it?
Sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas) is a dicotyledonous plant in the morning glory family, Convolvulaceae.
This American economist and social theorist, a prominent voice in the conservative movement, received the National Humanities Medal from President George W. Bush in 2002 — who is he?
Thomas Sowell (SOHL; born June 30, 1930) is an American economist, economic historian, and social theorist.

It spawned a maritime patrol version (the Tu-142) and even a passenger airliner (the Tu-114), and Russia expects to keep flying this propeller-driven bomber until at least 2040 — which aircraft is it?
Tupolev Tu-95 (NATO reporting name: "Bear") is a Soviet nuclear-capable large, four-engine turboprop strategic bomber and missile platform.
An American investor and philanthropist, he is the chairman of Berkshire Hathaway and, as of January 2026, the ninth-richest person in the world. Who is he?
Warren Buffett (born August 30, 1930) is an American investor and philanthropist who is the chairman and former CEO of the conglomerate Berkshire Hathaway.

This scientific discipline studies the structure, classification, behavior, and distribution of animals both living and extinct, and its name derives from the Greek word for 'animal' — name this field?
Zoology (zoh-, UK also zoo-) is the scientific study of animals.
Produced by oxidizing adrenaline and named for its deep violet color, this compound was studied in the mid-20th century as a possible cause of schizophrenia — what is it?
Adrenochrome: Chemical compound. It was the subject of limited research from the 1950s through to the 1970s as a potential cause of schizophrenia.

This American biologist founded a university institute for sex research in 1947 and gave his name to a scale measuring sexual orientation, after publishing landmark but controversial reports on human sexuality. Who was he?
Ectothermic four-limbed vertebrates whose only living members are frogs, salamanders, and the worm-like caecilians — what class of animal is this?
Amphibian: Class of ectothermic tetrapods. The origin of modern lissamphibians, which first appeared during the Early Triassic, around 250 million years ago, has long been contentious.
Nicknamed 'Nastia' in the USSR and known to NATO as 'Curl,' this twin-engine turboprop military transport was later license-built in China under a different name — what aircraft is it?
Antonov An-26: Soviet turboprop transport aircraft. It is the third member of the Antonov An-24 family, coming after the An-24 and An-30, while preceding the An-32 and cancelled An-132.
Ranking as the second-largest lizard species after the Komodo dragon, this excellent swimmer thrives in lakes, rivers, and even city sewers across South and Southeast Asia — what is it?
Asian water monitor: Species of lizard. The Asian water monitor (Varanus salvator) is a large varanid lizard native to South and Southeast Asia.
This fig tree spreads outward indefinitely by growing extra trunks from its own prop roots, and its most famous species is the national tree of India — what is it?
This red-orange breakdown product of heme colors feces brown and urine pale yellow as it's further broken down in the body — which compound?
Bilirubin: Red pigment of the bile.

A twin-engine, carrier-capable strike fighter flown by the U.S., Australia, and Kuwait, this larger, more advanced follow-on to an earlier 1980s Navy jet packs an internal 20 mm rotary cannon and can be rigged as an airborne refueling tanker — what is it called?
The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
Boeing F/A-18E/F Super Hornet: Series of carrier-based multirole combat aircraft.
Despite the name, this pseudocereal isn't related to true cereals at all — it's kin to rhubarb and sorrel, and was first cultivated in Yunnan around 6,000 BC — which crop is it?
Buckwheat: Species of flowering plant in the family Polygonaceae.
This suborder of 'dog-like' carnivores includes bears, raccoons, weasels, and seals, and is thought to have diversified mainly across North America and northern Eurasia — what's it called?
Caniformia: Suborder of mammals. Caniformia is a suborder within the order Carnivora consisting of "dog-like" carnivorans.
Named for barbels that resemble a cat's whiskers, these scaleless, ray-finned fish include giants like the Mekong species and go by nicknames such as 'mud cat' in the Southern US — what are they?
Catfish: Order of fish. Catfish are a diverse group of ray-finned fish of the order Siluriformes (historically Nematognathi).
Domesticated from the red junglefowl roughly 8,000 years ago, this bird now numbers over 26 billion worldwide, more than any other domesticated species — what is it?
Chicken: Domesticated subspecies of red junglefowl. The chicken (Gallus gallus domesticus) is the domesticated form of the red junglefowl (Gallus gallus), originally native to Southeast Asia.
Sold under the brand name Anafranil, this tricyclic antidepressant treats obsessive-compulsive disorder but also premature ejaculation and the cataplexy that comes with narcolepsy — which drug?
Clomipramine: Antidepressant. It has also been notably used to treat premature ejaculation and the cataplexy associated with narcolepsy.
Once classified among the thrushes, this small Old World flycatcher was later reassigned to the family Muscicapidae — which bird?
Common redstart: Species of bird. The common redstart (Phoenicurus phoenicurus), or often simply redstart, is a small passerine bird in the genus Phoenicurus.
First identified in Europe and interbreeding with Neanderthals as early as roughly 45,000 years ago, this term describes the earliest known modern humans on the continent — what are they called?
Cro-Magnon: Earliest anatomically modern humans in Europe and West Asia.
Nicknamed the 'Radioactive Boy Scout,' this Michigan teenager built a crude neutron source in a backyard shed while chasing his dream of a homemade nuclear reactor — who is he?
David Hahn: American nuclear radiation enthusiast (1976–2016)

This bacterial infection announces itself with a barking, croup-like cough and a tough grey or white "pseudomembrane" that slowly leathers over the throat and chokes the airway — what is this disease?
Diphtheria: Bacterial disease. Diphtheria is an infection caused by the bacterium Corynebacterium diphtheriae.
Nicknamed the spiny anteater, this quill-covered, egg-laying mammal from Australia and New Guinea has babies called puggles — which creature?

This anaerobic parasite infects tens of millions of people worldwide, causing a gut disease whose name comes from a word meaning tissue disintegration, and kills over 55,000 people each year — what is it?
With a glossy black head and a distinctive white bill shield, this rail-family waterbird is found from Europe to Australia — which bird?
Eurasian coot: Species of bird. The Eurasian coot (Fulica atra), also known as the common coot or Australian coot, is a member of the rail and crake bird family, the Rallidae.

An annual legume with leaves of three small leaflets, this semiarid crop has flavored dishes of the Indian subcontinent since ancient times — yet there's little clinical proof it works as the supplement people often take. What is it?
With a bushy tail, triangular ears, and a reputation for cunning that echoes through folklore worldwide, which small omnivorous canid lives on every continent except Antarctica?
One of Maxwell's equations, this application of the divergence theorem connects electric charge distribution to the electric field it creates. Which one is it?
Gauss's law: Foundational law of electromagnetism relating electric field and charge distributions.
Google's mailbox provider is the largest email service in the world. Roughly how many users does it have?
Gmail is a mailbox provider by Google and the largest email service worldwide, with 1.8 billion users.
After a record 43 years as crown prince, this Swedish monarch approved constitutional reforms stripping the crown of its remaining political powers shortly before his 1973 death. Who was he?
Gustaf VI Adolf: King of Sweden from 1950 to 1973.

Spun into usable fiber some 50,000 years ago and, alongside bamboo, among the fastest-growing plants on Earth, which Cannabis sativa crop is grown for rope, paper, textiles and biofuel rather than for getting high?
These giant wasps of the genus Vespa build communal nests from chewed wood pulp, with one Asian species growing past two inches long — what are they called?
This mammal order today includes only small African and Middle Eastern hyraxes, but once boasted a species weighing up to 600 kilograms called Titanohyrax — which order?
Hyracoidea: Order of mammals. It includes the living hyraxes, placed within the family Procaviidae, and several extinct taxa.

A functional gastrointestinal disorder characterized by abdominal pain, bloating, and changes in bowel movement consistency over long periods, sometimes years, it can negatively affect quality of life and is associated with anxiety and depression. What condition is this?
Irritable bowel syndrome: Functional gastrointestinal disorder. The cause of IBS is not known but multiple factors have been proposed to lead to the condition.
This British chemical engineer founded a major chemicals group in 1998 and later became a minority shareholder with control over football operations at Manchester United — who is he?
Jim Ratcliffe: British engineer and businessman (born 1952)
Named for a district in Turkey's Sivas Province, which large livestock guardian breed has been exported to Africa to protect flocks from cheetahs?
Kangal Shepherd Dog: Turkish breed of dog. The Kangal Shepherd Dog or Turkish Kangal (Turkish: Kangal Çoban Köpeği) is a traditional Turkish breed of large livestock guardian dog.
Native to North America and infamous for occasionally eating their mates after reproduction, the females of this venomous spider species sport striking black-and-red coloring — what species is it?
Latrodectus mactans: Species of spider. Latrodectus mactans, known as southern black widow or simply black widow, and the shoe-button spider, is a venomous species of spider in the genus Latrodectus.
This Australian speech and language therapist and amateur stage actor helped King George VI manage his stammer — who is he?
Lionel Logue: Australian speech and language therapist (1880–1953)
This flowering legume genus boasts over 199 species and has become such a successful invasive spreader in Iceland that it's now considered an ecological problem — which genus?
With horn-shaped fins on its head and one of the highest brain-to-body ratios of any fish, this filter-feeding giant may even recognize itself in a mirror — which creature?
Sold under the brand name Mobic, this NSAID in the oxicam family blocks COX-2 more strongly than COX-1 and ranked 27th among the most prescribed US medications in 2023. What drug is it?

An advanced modification of its Korean War-era predecessor, this Soviet transonic fighter — NATO reporting name 'Fresco' — was license-built in China and Poland, and remains in North Korean service today — which jet?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-17: Soviet jet fighter aircraft family.

Beginning as a tightly compressed gray sponge before expanding into a pitted yellow-brown honeycomb atop a hollow white stem, which springtime fungus is a prized edible found near old orchards and hardwoods?
Morchella esculenta: Species of fungus. The pits are rounded and irregularly arranged.
Sold under the brand name Deca-Durabolin, this anabolic steroid is prescribed for conditions like anemia and osteoporosis despite masculinizing side effects — which compound?
Nandrolone: Androgenic Anabolic steroid. Nandrolone, also known as 19-nortestosterone, is an endogenous androgen.
Element 102 honors the inventor of dynamite, who endowed a famous set of prizes — fitting, since this synthetic metal can only be forged in particle accelerators. What is it?
Nobelium: Chemical element with atomic number 102 (No)
In this learning process, voluntary behaviors are shaped by their consequences — strengthened by reinforcement, weakened by punishment or extinction. What is it called?
Operant conditioning: Type of associative learning process for behavioral modification.
This B vitamin's name comes from the Greek for "from everywhere," since it turns up in nearly all foods, and animals need it to build coenzyme A — what is it?
Derived from the Latin for 'by a hundred,' this dimensionless number expresses a ratio as a fraction of 100 and is usually written with a % sign — what is it called?

Percentage: Number or ratio expressed as a fraction of 100. In mathematics, a percentage, percent, or per cent (from Latin per centum 'by a hundred') is a number or ratio expressed as a fraction of 100.
Their name blends the Greek for "plant" and "drifter": these self-feeding plankton photosynthesize in the sunlit surface waters of oceans and lakes — what are they?
Phytoplankton: Autotrophic members of the plankton ecosystem.
Native to Southeast Asia and tasting like a sweet grapefruit, this non-hybrid citrus is the largest of them all — in fact, an ancestor of both the grapefruit and the bitter orange — what is it?
Pomelo: Citrus fruit from Southeast Asia.
Created in the early 18th century, this dark pigment was the first modern synthetic color, made by oxidizing iron ferrocyanide salts — what is it?
Prussian blue: Synthetic pigment. Prussian blue (also known as Berlin blue, Brandenburg blue, Parisian and Paris blue) is a dark blue pigment produced by oxidation of ferrous ferrocyanide salts.
Element 88 reacts with nitrogen rather than oxygen in air, turning black, and once glowed in self-luminous paints despite being highly carcinogenic — which element is it?
Radium: Chemical element with atomic number 88 (Ra)
Curving around the chest, these bones protect the lungs and heart and, in snakes, support and protect the whole body — what are they called?
Rib: Long bone in vertebrates that protects vital respiratory and cardiovascular organs.
First identified in Wuhan in late 2019 and once provisionally called 2019-nCoV, this positive-sense RNA virus is the one that causes COVID-19 — what's its official name?
SARS-CoV-2: Virus that causes COVID-19. The virus previously had the provisional name 2019 novel coronavirus (2019-nCoV), and has also been called human coronavirus 2019 (HCoV-19 or hCoV-19).
A month or so of a diet starved of vitamin C brings on this old deficiency disease — fatigue, sore limbs, and bleeding gums among its hallmarks. What is its scorbutic name?
Scurvy: Disease resulting from a lack of vitamin C.
Named after a Native American war chief, this four-blade, twin-engine Army helicopter entered service in 1979 to replace the Bell UH-1 Iroquois — which aircraft is it?
Sikorsky UH-60 Black Hawk: Series of military utility transport helicopters.

Found in Indonesia, Papua New Guinea, and northeastern Australia, this large flightless black bird is a close ratite relative of the emu and ostrich, and its Australian population is listed as endangered — which bird?
Southern cassowary: Species of flightless bird. It is one of the three living species of cassowary, alongside the dwarf cassowary and the northern cassowary.
This throat infection causes fever, red tonsils, and swollen neck glands, and can trigger a sandpaper-textured rash known as scarlet fever — which condition?
Streptococcal pharyngitis: Medical condition. It may be spread directly through touching infected sores.

This mammal family includes true digging specialists as well as aquatic desmans and the water-and-tunnel-adept star-nosed species, absent from Ireland but found from Eurasia to as far south as tropical Southeast Asian mountains — which family?
Talpidae: Family of small insectivorous mammals.
A cousin of caffeine found in trace amounts in tea, coffee, and chocolate, which methylxanthine drug is used to treat asthma and COPD by blocking adenosine receptors?
Theophylline: Drug used to treat respiratory diseases.
This central part of the body, from which the head, neck, limbs, and tail extend, is divided into chest, abdomen, and pelvic segments — which body part?

Torso: Central part of the living body. The tetrapod torso — including that of a human — can be divided into segments:

The chest or upper torso.

A reddish-purple natural dye secreted by sea snails in the Muricidae family, also called royal purple or imperial dye. The colored compound is 6,6'-dibromoindigo, extracted from snails like Bolinus brandaris. What is this ancient dye?
Tyrian purple: Natural dye extracted from Murex sea snails. The name Tyrian refers to the city of Tyre in ancient Phoenicia (modern-day Lebanon).
Native to southwestern Europe, this venomous viper is also called the asp or aspic viper, with about 4% of untreated bites proving fatal — which snake?
Vipera aspis: Species of snake. Its common names include asp, asp viper, European asp, and aspic viper, among others.

By measuring weak natural radioactivity with sensitive Geiger counters, this American chemist developed a dating method in 1949 that revolutionized archaeology — and won him a 1960 Nobel Prize. Who was he?
Known on the street as a date-rape drug but used medically to treat narcolepsy and cataplexy, this natural neurotransmitter is also a precursor to GABA in the brain — what compound is it?

Γ-Hydroxybutyric acid: Chemical compound. γ-Hydroxybutyric acid, also known as gamma-hydroxybutyric acid, GHB, or 4-hydroxybutanoic acid, is a naturally occurring neurotransmitter and a depressant drug.
Berkelium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for berkelium is Bk. Berkelium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Bk and atomic number 97.

Tim Burton: Timothy Walter Burton (born August 25, 1958) is an American filmmaker and animator.

Claire Danes: Claire Catherine Danes (born April 12, 1979) is an American actor.

Paul Walker: Paul William Walker IV (September 12, 1973 – November 30, 2013) was an American actor.
